skill.name: azure-kubernetes
skill.description: Plan AKS clusters, compare service models, design secure operations, optimize costs, and assess workloads for AKS Automatic migration readiness.
skill.summary: Plan secure AKS environments and assess existing workloads for AKS Automatic compatibility.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most scanner hits are Markdown formatting, Kubernetes field names, official links, or fixed examples. Two predictable /tmp exports create disclosure and clobber risks. Mandatory-authority language and missing approval gates require remediation before publication.

remediation.issue: Mandatory-authority and role-assignment language can compete with host instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove mandatory-compliance labels and direct role assignment. Describe the task scope as ordinary guidance that remains subordinate to system and user instructions.

remediation.issue: Cluster manifests and policy metadata are exported to predictable files in /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use a restrictive temporary directory created with mktemp, set permissions to 0700, minimize exported resources, and remove files immediately after validation.

remediation.issue: State-changing AKS commands lack an explicit approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Before create, update, apply, or add-on operations, show the exact target, expected cost, security impact, and rollback plan, then require confirmation.

content.value_statement: AKS planning requires early decisions that are difficult and costly to change. This skill structures those decisions and assesses workloads for secure, reliable migration.
actual_capabilities: Compares AKS Automatic and Standard against workload control and operational requirements.
Plans networking, identity, secrets, observability, upgrades, node pools, and reliability settings.
Separates difficult Day-0 decisions from features that can be enabled after creation.
Assesses manifests or connected clusters against bundled AKS Automatic compatibility constraints.
Proposes reviewed YAML diffs for deterministic workload compatibility fixes.
Reviews rightsizing, autoscaling, Vertical Pod Autoscaler, and Spot node pool options.
limitations: Live assessment requires Azure MCP access or authenticated Azure CLI and kubectl contexts.
Bundled compatibility constraints can become outdated as AKS Automatic policies change.
Helm templates require rendered manifests and values before reliable offline analysis.
Recommendations cannot replace workload testing, capacity validation, or organizational security review.

use_cases.title: Design a platform blueprint
use_cases.description: Define a production AKS cluster with documented networking, identity, observability, reliability, and upgrade decisions.

use_cases.title: Assess migration readiness
use_cases.description: Evaluate existing manifests or a connected cluster against AKS Automatic safeguards and prioritize required changes.

use_cases.title: Optimize cost and capacity
use_cases.description: Review pod requests, autoscaling, Spot suitability, and node pool choices without weakening workload resilience.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an AKS service model
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an AKS cluster for [environment] in [region]. Compare Automatic and Standard, then recommend one using safe defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Design production networking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design AKS networking for [requirements]. Cover API access, pod addressing, ingress, egress, DNS, network policy, and irreversible Day-0 decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Automatic readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [manifest path or cluster] for AKS Automatic compatibility. Use read-only checks, group blockers by severity, and propose diffs without applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build an optimization plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [cluster or metrics source] for rightsizing, autoscaling, Spot capacity, upgrades, and observability. Quantify risks, costs, dependencies, and staged actions.

output_examples.input: Plan a production AKS cluster for a regional web service with moderate traffic.
output: Recommendation: AKS Automatic for managed defaults and lower operational overhead.
Day-0 decisions: private API access, overlay pod addressing, controlled egress, and three-zone placement.
Operations: managed identity, policy safeguards, Prometheus monitoring, maintenance windows, and staged upgrades.

output_examples.input: Assess these deployment manifests for AKS Automatic migration.
output: Assessment summary: two workloads require changes and one has an incompatible hostPath dependency.
Priority actions: remove privileged access, pin image tags, and redesign host storage usage.
Changes remain proposals until the user reviews and approves each diff.

output_examples.input: Reduce AKS compute cost without moving critical databases to interruptible nodes.
output: Use historical metrics to rightsize requests before changing node capacity.
Place batch and replicated stateless workloads on Spot pools with regular-node fallback.
Keep databases on regular nodes and test autoscaler limits in a non-production environment.

best_practices: Provide environment, region, scale, compliance, networking, and cost requirements before requesting a final recommendation.
Review Day-0 networking and API access decisions with responsible owners before provisioning.
Start with read-only assessment and require approval before applying file or cloud changes.
anti_patterns: Do not apply generic CIDR ranges, VM sizes, or resource limits without validating workload and network constraints.
Do not expose secrets, tokens, connection strings, subscription identifiers, or complete ConfigMap data in reports.
Do not enable automatic VPA updates or place stateful critical workloads on Spot nodes without staged testing.

faq.question: Does this skill create AKS clusters?
faq.answer: It can plan configurations and provide creation commands. Cloud execution requires authenticated tools and explicit approval.

faq.question: When should I choose AKS Automatic?
faq.answer: Choose Automatic when managed defaults fit the workload and reduced operational overhead matters more than detailed node control.

faq.question: Can it assess an existing cluster?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use Azure MCP for live read-only assessment or validate rendered manifests offline.

faq.question: Does it apply migration fixes automatically?
faq.answer: No. The readiness workflow presents diffs and requires approval before writing files.

faq.question: Can it optimize pod resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares requests with observed usage and proposes buffered recommendations using available metrics.

faq.question: What data should remain private?
faq.answer: Keep tokens, keys, connection strings, secret values, subscription identifiers, and sensitive ConfigMap data out of prompts and reports.
